newsitem.title: UK: LME copper claws higher in late office trading.
newsitem.headline: LME copper claws higher in late office trading.

text.p: LME three months copper pushed gently higher in late inter-office trading on Friday but steered clear of the day's highs.

Earlier, a brisk rally sparked by technical buying and aggressive shortcovering pushed copper to a fresh 8-1/2 month high of $2,375 per tonne but then values backed off to end at $2,366, $38 up on Thursday's kerb close.
At 1900 GMT copper was indicated at $2,367/2,372.
Analysts said copper's break above $2,350 pointed to continued gains and suggested prices could now target the $2,400 psychological level.
Expecatations that Chinese demand was on the rise in the near term could also tighten the market, they added.
Aluminium remained roughly around its kerb close of $1,631, $24 firmer than on Thursday, and was last indicated at $1,628/1,630.
Other base metals were little changed.
